doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Father's roots and riding the Jim Crow car on family rail trips
summary: Father was born in Indianapolis, mother in Mississippi; David Baker asks about Jim Crow travel and Johnson says the family just accepted it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: My dad was a native Indianapolis. He was born here in Indianapolis, Indiana. My mother was from West Point, Mississippi. My dad was born here in Indianapolis. My best recollection is [that] his dad and mother were born here in Indianapolis.

Jay, let me ask you, when your dad traveled and you guys [the family] traveled, how did that affect having to travel in the Jim Crow car? Were you exempted from that as a result of your dad having the passes?
No. The Jim Crow thing was the Jim Crow thing, and my best recollection is [that] we just accepted it.
Yeah, well, there were not a lot of alternatives.
No, there weren’t any alternatives, right? So the black people were in one section and the white people were in another section. It was just a way of life.
